text:
jamie: deploybot blocked rc9 canary for svc-search — integrity_scan failed. holding release notes + PR merge. details from deploybot below. anyone from security available?

deploybot: [scan-id: 2823456789-1] INTEGRITY_SCAN: HIGH - transitive lib 'libcryptoX' flagged (CVE-2025-9999). SBOM provenance mismatch: base image missing signature. Actions: hold release_notes, quarantine canary, tag image as quarantined. Logs: `sbom-verify --image gcr.io/myorg/svc-search:rc9` -> signature: MISSING.

alex: ack. can we do a quick pin to previous base image and retry canary?

sasha: I grabbed the last green digest and attempted a repin, but the binary linked to libcryptoX is baked in the layer. quick pin won't fix the transitive package inside our pip wheel.

security: do not merge release notes or GA until triage finished. initial triage: the CVE is a crypto side-channel in an optional native extension but we need reproduction steps. if exploitability is low for our config we can consider an exception; otherwise we need a patch or pin of the library version.

maria: proposal: revert canary traffic to `release/v0.9.7` and open `hotfix/rc9-libcrypto-patch`. That buys us the change-window window to triage and prepare a patched build. If security signs off, we can re-run the canary in the open change window.

jamie: change window opens in ~2h. if vuln triage isn't done by then we should delay GA. who can own the hotfix branch?

alex: assigning myself to hotfix branch. plan: fork rc9 -> hotfix/rc9-libcrypto; run `pip wheel --no-binary :all: libcryptoX==1.2.3` and rebuild runtime image. If vulnerability present in our wheel we either vendor patched code or bump to upstream patched release.

sasha: starting regression repro now. attaching short logs:```
$ docker run --rm gcr.io/myorg/svc-search:rc9 
# crash output truncated
ImportError: cannot open shared object file: libcryptoX.so.1.1
```

security: uploading triage notes to shared drive (link: https://short.link/triage-282345). If exploit requires access to internal KMS or specific runtime flags we can classify as low-risk for GA; still need legal sign-off for SBOM provenance mismatch.

deploybot: Action taken: release_notes locked by deploybot; merge queue paused for this PR. Override allowed only with tag `security:approved` from user in `security` group or after a successful re-run of `INTEGRITY_SCAN` with status PASS. Quarantine tag applied: `quarantine/rc9-282345`.

maria: I'll prep a one-line release note hold message we can paste in the changelog so marketing has context. Suggest: "GA delayed: integrity scan escalation under triage; will update in change window."

alex: command for pinning (ops): `gcloud artifacts docker images add-tag gcr.io/myorg/svc-search@sha256:0a1b2c3d release/v0.9.7-canary-temp --quiet` — use this to route canary traffic back. confirmed we can revert traffic in <10m.

jamie: thanks. marque: @security please mark ETA for triage? we need to decide delay vs hotfix vs pin by T+90m.

security: triage SME pinged, ETA ~45m. legal looped for SBOM provenance, they want the verification evidence before exception.

sasha: repro run done, attaching more logs to the triage doc. initial note: vuln surfaces only when `LD_PRELOAD` is set and we don't set that in production path; still need deeper static analysis. :eyes: 

jamie: OK. plan for now: 1) Alex opens hotfix/rc9-libcrypto-patch and starts rebuild. 2) Maria rewrites release note hold. 3) Sasha continues repro + posts evidence to triage doc. 4) Security returns with final verdict; if PASS we re-run canary and unlock notes. If FAIL we keep quarantine and schedule QA patch rollout.

alex: hotfix branch created and pipeline triggered `ci/hotfix-rc9-libcrypto` (build #482).

deploybot: CI triggered: canary traffic reverted to release/v0.9.7-canary-temp. Quarantine remains.

jamie: fine — keep me posted. if triage slips past change window we bump GA and update release notes with a short postmortem. :rotating_light: 

security: will update triage doc asap. tagging `security:escalated` in thread once SME responds.

maria: post done to marketing ops with holding blurb.

jamie: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread as the single source of truth for decisions on rc9.
